item.title: Working Across Political Divides: Pakistan’s Strategy in the UN Security Council
item.description:
In an exclusive interview with PassBlue, Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, Pakistan's permanent representative to the United Nations and an elected member of the Security Council, outlined Islamabad's approach to global peace and security while highlighting his country’s expectations for the high-level week of the General Assembly’s 81st session. Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to speak on Sept. 25.
Ahmad, who met with PassBlue on Sept. 11 at Pakistan’s mission to the UN, described his country’s mediating role in the Iran-US war that erupted on Feb. 28. With the Security Council unable to act quickly, Ahmad said, Pakistan drew on its longstanding ties with both countries to help secure a ceasefire at the peak of fighting and within weeks. That effort culminated in face-to-face talks in Islamabad, the highest-level engagement between the two countries in more than four decades, he added, saying that Pakistan has been trying to “convince the parties to come back to the negotiating table.” (Ahmad was named foreign secretary of Pakistan on Sept. 9.)

item.title: Escalating conflict drives new displacement in Yemen
item.description: The escalating conflict in Yemen is choking off aid shipments and driving fresh displacement, including to nearby Djibouti, with UN agencies reporting on Tuesday that nearly 100,000 people have been displaced since fighting intensified earlier this month.

item.title: Ebola responders grapple with widening outbreak in DR Congo
item.description: The deadly Ebola virus outbreak in DR Congo continues to spread across the vast country despite some success in containing it, aid officials said on Tuesday, in a renewed call for international support to help responders on the ground.

item.title: Back to school in Haiti: ‘Madame, can you stop what the gangs are doing to us?’
item.description: When UNICEF’s Representative in Haiti Geetanjali Narayan stepped into a classroom in Port-au-Prince at the start of the new school year, she asked the children a simple question: What did they most need from the UN children’s agency?

item.title: Ukraine: Attacks on education threaten an entire generation, UNICEF warns
item.description: In an underground classroom in Sumy, Ukraine, children sit quietly at their desks, busy with the day’s lessons. For the moment they are shielded from the horrors of nearly five years of war, but just barely.

item.title: World fears major war more than any other global risk, UN survey finds
item.description: Two years ago, the idea of a large-scale war breaking out felt like a distant hypothetical to the experts who help chart the world’s dangers. Today it tops their list of fears, according to a new UN Global Risk Report.

item.title: Gaza remains recovery points to possible war crimes, says UN rights chief
item.description: Bodies are still being pulled from the rubble of Gaza, three years after Israeli bombardment flattened entire neighbourhoods – most of them women and children.

item.title: ‘Super El Niño’ deepens hunger crisis in South Sudan – WFP
item.description: The already dire hunger crisis in South Sudan is becoming increasingly critical as violence, extreme weather and dwindling aid leave millions without enough food, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Tuesday.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Rising violence triggers emergency meeting on Yemen
item.description: Amid rising violence in Yemen, the Security Council has called an emergency meeting at 3pm (NY time) on Tuesday to discuss the situation in the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait shipping route as UN agencies warn of rising displacement, including thousands of Yemenis fleeing to Djibouti. item.title: UNICEF says thousands of children require mental health support after Nepal floods
item.description: Three weeks after the devastating flash floods in Nepal, about 17,000 children require urgent mental health and psychosocial support in the country, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday.
